title: Static flat connections make the raw moving-radius budget diverge despite exact finite-energy dynamics

flat_connection_test.background: On a periodic three-torus in temporal gauge take A(t,x)=a with nonzero constant vector a and E=-partial_t A=0. Then div A=0 and the K1573 coefficient is B_A=|e||a|.
flat_connection_test.budget_divergence: For every nonzero a, int_0^T B_A dt=|e||a|T and int_0^infinity B_A dt=infinity. The transparent K1573 choice rho'=-(C_m/4)B_A therefore spends every finite initial radius in finite time.
flat_connection_test.finite_energy_control: The background itself has zero Maxwell curvature and finite (indeed zero curvature) energy. Charged linear matter on it has a positive conserved covariant energy, so no physical growth or singularity is forced by the divergent raw budget.
flat_connection_test.global_gauge_boundary: A constant a is removable by a periodic U(1) gauge exactly when its holonomies are integral: e a_j L_j belongs to 2pi Z for every torus period L_j. Generic a is a genuine flat holonomy and cannot be dismissed as a periodic pure gauge.
flat_connection_test.consequence: Uniform Sobolev control or conservation alone cannot prove B_A in L1_t. The K1573 radius budget is sufficient but not necessary and is structurally non-sharp on the harmonic flat-connection sector.
flat_connection_test.scope_guard: This counterexample does not disprove local moving-radius control, exclude an integrable oscillatory remainder, or settle the nonlinear Maxwell-scalar flow.
